Subsequently, the Petitioner filed an appeal before APTEL, bearing Appeal No. 254 of 2024 ( _NHPC Limited vs CERC_ ). At present, the said appeal is sub-judice. In compliance, Respondents Nos. 6 and 5, BSES Yamuna Power Limited (BYPL) and BSES Rajdhani Power Limited (BRPL), respectively, filed their replies vide affidavits dated 18.8.2025 and 24.9.2025, respectively, to the present petition filed vide affidavit dated 26.11.2024. In response, the Petitioner vide separate affidavit dated 29.9.2025, filed its rejoinder thereto. The Respondent No.7, TPDDL, filed its reply, vide affidavit dated 18.8.2025, to the additional information filed by the Petitioner vide affidavit dated 18.6.2025. Further, the Petitioner, in compliance with the ROP dated 7.8.2025, filed the additional information vide affidavit dated 5.9.2025. None of the Respondents has filed its reply, despite notice. 8. The Petitioner has submitted that the additional capitalisation on account of arbitration cases with respect to works associated with M/s CCL (Rs. 159.52 lakh and Rs. 18.76 lakh) and M/s JAL (Rs. 1035.00 lakh) was settled in 2019-20 and 2021-22, respectively, pursuant to court orders. Further, reimbursement of interest amounting to Rs. 890.91 lakh on the aforesaid principal payment, including Rs. 178.27 lakh to M/s CCL, has already been allowed by the order dated 30.11.2022 in Petition No. 145/GT/2020. Accordingly, it has prayed that the same be reimbursed for the interest amount of Rs. 1979.87 lakh on the settlement of the claim of M/s JAL. 101. In response, the Petitioner has clarified that it has prudently placed on record the relevant documents along with a detailed justification by affidavit dated 18.6.2025. 102. The Respondent, Rajasthan Discoms, has submitted that the Petitioner has claimed interest of Rs. 1979.87 lakh, relying on the Commission’s earlier allowance of Rs. 890.91 lakh in Petition No. 145/GT/2020. It is contended that the Petitioner has repeatedly pursued arbitration claims without adopting a clear policy, resulting in prolonged litigation and avoidable financial burden. The dispute with Jaiprakash Associates Ltd., pending since 1993, exemplifies this lapse, where a timely settlement was possible but not pursued. Such inaction has led to interest liability nearly four times the principal, reflecting inefficient liability management. The burden of this lapse cannot be transferred to beneficiaries, as recovery on such grounds violates principles of prudence and accountability. Accordingly, the Petitioner’s claim is liable to be rejected. 104.
